speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and have abnormal leg positioning following a rear-end collision. To assess the extent of your injury, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and whether you heard a "pop" or felt a snap at the time of the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) tear and Right Hip Dislocation.

The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision as a restrained driver) combined with immediate pain in the groin and knees suggests a high-energy trauma affecting the hip joint and knee ligaments. Can you confirm if your right leg is currently stuck in a specific position, such as being shortened and externally rotated?
